I just now learned that ICANN also controls IPs. Until reading your comment and looking it up, I thought that they were just about DNS.

Not directly.

ICANN's practical power over IPv4 is very limited, and these are all IPv4 addresses we're looking at (e.g. "important IP address" threads going up on Voat). IPv6 is undergoing very, very slow adoption, which will likely be forced due to the IoT. But basically speaking, ICANN allocates IP addresses in large blocks, and those blocks are doled out by whoever manages to claim them, and those are then subdivided up more, etc. until you get, say, voat.co. Thing is though that IPv4 is used up so far as ICANN is concerned. All they directly deal in now, AFAIK, is IPv6 in terms of block allocation. Although there are a few groups and entities with mostly-unused blocks that have, in a rather civic-minded gesture, returned the unused portions (or the entire block) to ICANN for re-assignment, those are the exceptions, not the norm, and won't help forever even assuming they are reassigned properly.

Plus, if this becomes the censorious dystopia we all fear, it's going to take time for that to happen. They don't get to just press a 'kill switch' on anything that displeases them, or at least, they don't get to do that just yet.
